I need to develop a detailed, step‑by‑step migration strategy for moving our on‑premises customer database to a cloud platform while meeting GDPR and PCI‑DSS compliance. This is a very broad, multi-domain question that spans technical, legal, and operational concerns. To answer it properly I need to break the overall lifecycle into a structured sequence of stages, and for each stage identify:
1. The core goal/activity
2. Regulatory touch-points that are relevant
3. Tools or controls that satisfy GDPR and PCI-DSS
4. Validation gates or artifacts that show continuous compliance

Key regulatory articles/requirements I should weave in:
- GDPR: Lawfulness, purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, security/confidentiality (Art.5, 32), DPIA (Art 35), SCCs or other transfer mechanism if moving out of EEA, breach notification (Art 33-34)
- PCI-DSS: Network segmentation, encryption (in motion & at rest), access control (Principles 3,4,8), vulnerability/pen testing (Req.11), logging & monitoring (Req.10), incident response (Req.12)

Lifecycle stages that make sense:
0. Governance & pre-work
1. Assessment of source data & regulatory scope
2. Cloud vendor & architecture selection
3. Network & security foundation
4. Protective controls design
5. Data minimisation & classification
6. Migration execution
7. Post-migration validation & sign-off
8. Ongoing operations & continuous compliance

For a migration project the first 0-4 activities usually happen before any data touches the cloud; 5 is iterative; 6 is the shortest but highest-risk period; 7-8 turn the new system into steady-state BAU.

I need to make sure every stage has concrete compliance checks rather than just "document everything".
</tool_response>

Below is a concise, field-ready migration playbook you can drop directly into your project-management or compliance tool.  
It is structured into eight sequential stages (0–7), each paired with a validation gate and “Regulatory Evidence Checklist” that can be collected for auditors to demonstrate continuous GDPR & PCI-DSS compliance.

──────────────────────────
0. Governance & Pre-work (Week 0–2)  
Goal: Build the legal & governance scaffold before anyone touches data.  
Key actions  
• Appoint cloud DPO (Art. 37) and PCI DSS compliance owner.  
• Confirm all existing legal bases for processing (Art. 6, 9).  
• Execute DPIA (Art. 35) and PCI scoping workbook.  
• Sign SCC or equivalent for any out-of-EEA data residency.  
Validation gate / evidence  
□ DPIA signed off → artefact for (Art 35)  
□ Responsibility matrix (RACI) stored in compliance system.

──────────────────────────
1. Source & Scope Discovery (Week 3–4)  
Goal: Know exactly what you’re lifting.  
Key actions  
• Classify every entity in the customer DB: Personal / Sensitive / CHD / PAN / Token only.  
• Map data flows & retention limits (Art. 5-1e, Req. 3.1).  
• Quantify delete-flags and archived rows (important to avoid transferring “stale” data).  
Validation gate / evidence  
□ Signed data-flow diagram & data-inventory spreadsheet.  
□ Retention schedule attested by DPO.

──────────────────────────
2. Cloud Region & Vendor Selection (Week 4–5)  
Goal: Pick providers that already satisfy PCI-DSS & GDPR.  
Key actions  
• Require SOC2-Type-II + PCI-DSS AoC + DPA with SCC.  
• Prefer in-region-homed services for escrow & easier GDPR guidance.  
• Validate IAAS vs PAAS scope (limits your PCI CDE footprint).  
Validation gate / evidence  
□ AoC + PCI-DSS ROC artefacts reviewed and committed to vendor artifact vault.  
□ GDPR Data-Processing Agreement countersigned & stored.

──────────────────────────
3. Network & Segmentation Foundation (Week 6–7)  
Goal: Build “PCI-isolation by design” before any data lands.  
Key actions  
• Deploy dual-VPC: PCI-VPC (CDE) and non-PCI VPC.  
• Enforce TLS 1.2+ everywhere; private-link / IPSec back to on-prem.  
• Add WAF, DDoS Shield, and subnet Proxy explicit-allow.  
Validation gate / evidence  
□ PCI DSS Network Diagram (Req. 1.1) delivered and approved by QSA.  
□ Packet-capture test evidencing encrypted transport (Req.4.1).

──────────────────────────
4. Controls Architecture (Week 7–8)  
Goal: Translate regulatory articles into technical guard-rails.  
Key actions  
A. GDPR PAN/Token vault w/ customer symmetric key stored in Cloud-KMS-HSM (Art. 32)  
B. MFA for every IAM entity (PCI 8.2, GDPR Art 32).  
C. Fine-grained RBAC mapped to roles-to-data-lists documented in IAM catalog.  
D. Central log sink (Cloud-SIEM) immutable 13-month retention (PCI Req. 10.7).  
Validation gate / evidence  
□ Policy-as-Code pipeline installs above IAM, encryption, retention rules.  
□ CIS or NIST-run benchmark automated tests > 90 % green.

──────────────────────────
5. Data Minimisation & Classification (Iterative, parallel, Week 5–8)  
Goal: Transform & anonymise before copy.  
Key actions  
• Anonymise/pseud fields where legal; drop data past retention period.  
• Sensitive data double-blind encryption: TLS-1-RTT between on-prem & CSP, KMS keys never exported.  
• Tokenise PAN using vault service rather than direct replication (shifts QS scope).  
Validation gate / evidence  
□ Running Anonymisation pipeline shows <10 % of original personal data carried forward.  
□ Vault token reconciliation report signed off by compliance owner.

──────────────────────────
6. Secure Migration Execution (Week 8–10)  
Goal: Perform the move with zero data-leakage and roll-back options.  
Technical workflow  
a. Freeze on-prem DB into read-only logs.  
b. Pipeline: Full-Backup → S3 encrypted bucket → cloud VM → CASB scan.  
c. Delta-stream via change-data-capture until cut-over.  
d. Dual-write during parallel-run phase (< 72 h).  
Compliance touch-points  
• Every backup file checked against SHA-256 manifest.  
• View-by-view verification of tokenisation mappings.  
• Log every copy event in immutable SIEM.  
Validation gate / evidence  
□ Successful CASB-mandated DLP scan on destination bucket (no CHD outside CDE).  
□ Post-“go-live” QSA spot-check shows PAN still vaulted.

──────────────────────────
7. Post-Migration Validation & Sign-off (Weeks 11-12)  
Goal: Prove you still meet GDPR necessity & PCI CDE segmentation.  
Activities  
• QSA onsite validation test: network segmentation + cardholder data flow tests.  
• Residency/ownership fingerprint dump to GDPR supervisory authority.  
• Update Record of Processing Activities (RoPA).  
• Schedule quarterly ASV vulnerability scan & PCI pen-test (Req.11).  
Validation gate / evidence  
□ PCI ROC signed; AoC renewed.  
□ GDPR “congratulatory” letter from DPO stored with dpiareference.  
□ Incident-response run-book updated and tested.

──────────────────────────
8. Ongoing Continuous Compliance  
• Deploy weekly config-drift guardrails via policy-as-code pipelines.  
• SQL Vulnerability scans monthly.  
• Rotate customer KMS keys every 365 days with 0-downtime key-versioning.  
• Quarterly Board-level review of Data Subject Request KPI & PCI KPI dashboards.

By treating every stage above as a mini-project with built-in evidence artefacts, you will satisfy audit questions before they arise and de-risk the migration itself.
